verses.sanskrit: श्रीरामचन्द्र उवाच — माण्डूक्यमेकमेवालं मुमुक्षूणां विमुक्तये | अन्येषामुपनिषदां पाठनं फलदं भवेत् ||
verses.transliteration: śrīrāmacandra uvāca — māṇḍūkyamekamevālaṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ vimuktaye | anyeṣāmupaniṣadāṃ pāṭhanaṃ phaladaṃ bhavet ||
verses.translation: Sri Ramachandra said: The Mandukya alone is quite sufficient for the liberation of those who seek liberation. The study of the other Upanishads becomes fruitful (as well).
verses.hindi: श्रीरामचन्द्र ने कहा: मुमुक्षुओं की मुक्ति के लिए अकेला माण्डूक्य ही पर्याप्त है। अन्य उपनिषदों का पाठ भी फलदायी है।
verses.commentary: The most provocative opening in all Upanishadic literature. Rama — speaking as the ultimate teacher — does not recommend a vast curriculum. He says: one text is enough. The Mandukya Upanishad in 12 verses maps the entire territory of consciousness (waking, dream, deep sleep, and turiya — the fourth), establishes AUM as the symbol of this totality, and identifies the individual self with Brahman. Rama's claim is not anti-intellectual — he immediately affirms that study of all 108 is also fruitful. But he refuses to make liberation contingent on vast scholarship. The gateway is always narrow, always close, always now.

verses.sanskrit: मनोनाशो विचारेण भवत्येव न संशयः | वासनानां क्षयो भूयस्ततो मोक्षो न चान्यथा ||
verses.transliteration: manonāśo vicāreṇa bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ | vāsanānāṃ kṣayo bhūyastato mokṣo na cānyathā ||
verses.translation: The dissolution of the mind occurs through enquiry — there is no doubt about this. The exhaustion of vasanas (deep impressions/tendencies) follows from this. Liberation comes from that — not otherwise.
verses.hindi: मन का नाश विचार से ही होता है — इसमें कोई सन्देह नहीं। उससे वासनाओं का क्षय होता है। उससे ही मोक्ष है — अन्यथा नहीं।
verses.commentary: Rama gives Hanuman the precise mechanism of liberation in two steps: (1) manonasha — dissolution of the mind, achieved through vicara (enquiry, self-investigation); (2) vasana-kshaya — exhaustion of the deep impressions (vasanas) that perpetuate the mind's conditioning. Liberation is not a sudden external event; it is the result of sustained investigation that progressively dissolves the habitual tendencies that create the illusion of a separate, suffering self. "Not otherwise" (na cānyathā) — Rama closes every escape route: there is no shortcut that bypasses genuine enquiry.

verses.sanskrit: योगश्चित्तवृत्तिरोधो योगो मोक्षप्रदायकः | योगः सर्वबन्धानां योगो मुक्तिसमाश्रयः ||
verses.transliteration: yogaścittavṛttirodho yogo mokṣapradāyakaḥ | yogaḥ sarvabandhānāṃ yogaḥ muktisamāśrayaḥ ||
verses.translation: Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications; yoga gives liberation. Yoga cuts all bonds; yoga rests on liberation.
verses.hindi: योग चित्त-वृत्तियों का निरोध है; योग मोक्ष देता है। योग सभी बंधनों को काटता है; योग मुक्ति पर आश्रित है।
verses.commentary: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of liberation. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of mukti.
verses.wordMeaning: The definition of yoga from Yoga Sutras, placed in the context of liberation. Yoga is the cessation of mental modifications, leading to liberation. All bonds are cut through this practice, which rests on the foundation of mukti.

verses.sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि न त्वं भूतिर्न च भूतानि | सर्वं मुक्ति एव सर्वं मुक्ति मयि सर्वम् ||
verses.transliteration: ahaṃ brahmāsmi na tvaṃ bhūtirna ca bhūtāni | sarvaṃ mukti eva sarvaṃ mukti mayi sarvam ||
verses.translation: I am Brahman, not you; I am birth, not beings; all is liberation alone, all is liberation in me.
verses.hindi: मैं ब्रह्म हूँ, तुम नहीं; मैं जन्म हूँ, प्राणी नहीं; सब मुक्ति ही है, सब मुक्ति मेरे में है।
verses.commentary: The declaration of non-duality with liberation as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is liberation; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.
verses.wordMeaning: The declaration of non-duality with liberation as the supreme. The individual Self is Brahman; the world is liberation; all distinctions dissolve in this recognition.

verses.sanskrit: यथा नदी समुद्रेषु यथा दीपो दीतेषु | तथा जीवो मुक्तौ लीनो न तत्र संशयो भवति ||
verses.transliteration: yathā nadī samudreṣu yathā dīpo dīpiteṣu | tathā jīvo muktau līno na tatra saṃśayo bhavati ||
verses.translation: As rivers merge into the ocean, as lamps merge into light — so the individual self merges into liberation. There is no doubt about this.
verses.hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में लीन हो जाती हैं, जैसे दीप ज्योति में लीन हो जाते हैं — वैसे ही जीव मुक्ति में लीन हो जाता है। इसमें कोई संशय नहीं।
verses.commentary: The dissolution of individuality into liberation. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution of individuality into liberation. The images of rivers into ocean and lamps into light illustrate the loss of separate identity while the essence remains.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं मुक्ति नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ mukti nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual liberation — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत मुक्ति — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of liberation: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of liberation: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो मुक्तिं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo muktiṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows liberation in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो मुक्ति को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

verses.sanskrit: मण्डूकः सर्वसारोऽयं सर्वोपनिषदां रहः | सर्ववेदान्तसारश्च नात्र कार्या विचारणा ||
verses.transliteration: maṇḍūkaḥ sarvasāro'yaṃ sarvopaniṣadāṃ rahaḥ | sarvāvedāntasāraśca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
verses.translation: The Mandukya is the essence of everything, the secret of all Upanishads, and the essence of all Vedanta. No deliberation need be made about this.
verses.hindi: माण्डूक्य सबका सार है, सभी उपनिषदों का रहस्य है, और सम्पूर्ण वेदान्त का सार है। इसमें कोई विचार करने की आवश्यकता नहीं।
verses.commentary: The Muktika's most compact summary of its thesis. The Mandukya is not merely one among 108 — it is the secret (rahasya) that the other 107 point toward. The 108 Upanishads are 108 approaches to the same territory. The Mandukya maps that territory most directly. Rama says "nātra kāryā vicāraṇā" — no deliberation is needed. This is not the closing of inquiry but the recognition that some truths are not arrived at by argument; they are recognised by direct seeing. The Mandukya invites you to see — now, directly — what is always already present.
verses.wordMeaning: The Muktika's most compact summary of its thesis. The Mandukya is not merely one among 108 — it is the secret (rahasya) that the other 107 point toward. verses.sanskrit: अष्टोत्तरशतं तेषां नामान्यपि वदाम्यहम् | येषां श्रवणमात्रेण सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ||
verses.transliteration: aṣṭottaraśataṃ teṣāṃ nāmānyapi vadāmyaham | yeṣāṃ śravaṇamātreṇa sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
verses.translation: I shall also declare the names of those one hundred and eight — by the mere hearing of whose names one is freed from all sins.
verses.hindi: उन एक सौ आठ (उपनिषदों) के नाम मैं कहता हूँ — जिनके केवल नाम सुनने मात्र से सभी पापों से मुक्ति हो जाती है।
verses.commentary: The Muktika's transition into the canonical list. The number 108 is not arbitrary — it is one of the most geometrically and astronomically significant numbers in the Hindu tradition: the ratio of the Sun's distance from Earth to the Sun's diameter is approximately 108; same for the Moon. The distance from Earth to the Sun is approximately 108 times the Sun's diameter. The 108 names of the divine, the 108 beads of the mala, the 108 Upanishads — all invoke this number as the symbol of cosmic completeness. The universe's fundamental proportions are encoded in the canon.
verses.wordMeaning: The Muktika's transition into the canonical list. The number 108 is not arbitrary — it is one of the most geometrically and astronomically significant numbers in the Hindu tradition: the ratio of the Sun's distance from Earth to the Sun's diameter is approximately 108; same for the Moon. The distance from Earth to the Sun is approximately 108 times the Sun's diameter. verses.sanskrit: सर्वत्र समदर्शित्वं सर्वभूतहिते रतिः | समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च एवं मुक्तः स उच्यते ||
verses.transliteration: sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratiḥ | samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca evaṃ muktaḥ sa ucyate ||
verses.translation: One who sees equally everywhere; who is devoted to the welfare of all beings; who is the same toward enemy and friend — such a one is called liberated.
verses.hindi: जो सर्वत्र समान दृष्टि रखता है; जो सभी प्राणियों के हित में प्रीति रखता है; जो शत्रु और मित्र में समान है — ऐसे को मुक्त कहते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Muktika's portrait of the jivanmukta — and it is entirely ethical and relational. Liberation is not described in terms of meditative states, supernatural powers, or philosophical knowledge. It is described in terms of how one relates to others: samadarshitva (equal vision everywhere), sarvabhuta-hite rati (love for the welfare of all beings), sama toward enemy and friend. The liberated person is recognised not by their inner experience but by the quality of their presence in the world. This is the Muktika's most practical teaching.

verses.sanskrit: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति | हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ||
verses.transliteration: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati | haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate ||
verses.translation: Desire is never quenched by the enjoyment of desired objects — just as fire grows ever larger when fed with oblations.
verses.hindi: कामनाएँ कामना-वस्तुओं के उपभोग से कभी शान्त नहीं होतीं — जैसे अग्नि आहुति डालने से और भी बढ़ती है।
verses.commentary: Quoted by Rama from the Manusmriti (2.94) and the Mahabharata, this verse is the Muktika's explanation of why ordinary desire-satisfaction cannot produce liberation. The fire analogy is precise: oblations (havis) are the fuel offered into the sacrificial fire, which they feed rather than extinguish. Every satisfied desire creates the template for a stronger desire. This is not an argument against enjoyment but an argument against the strategy of seeking liberation through satisfaction. The jivanmukta does not suppress desire — they no longer require its satisfaction for peace.

verses.sanskrit: शान्तं शिवमद्वैतं मुक्ति नित्यं शुद्धमच्युतम् | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: śāntaṃ śivamadvaitaṃ mukti nityaṃ śuddhamacyutam | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Peaceful, auspicious, non-dual liberation — eternal, pure, immutable. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: शांत, शिव, अद्वैत मुक्ति — नित्य, शुद्ध, अच्युत। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The attributes of liberation: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.
verses.wordMeaning: The attributes of liberation: peaceful, auspicious, non-dual, eternal, pure, immutable. Knowledge is seeing; ignorance is blindness.

verses.sanskrit: एको देवो द्वितीयो नास्ति यो मुक्तिं वेद तत्त्वतः | सोऽहमस्मि न किंचिद्भूतो न मृत्युर्न शोको न तथा ||
verses.transliteration: eko devo dvitīyo nāsti yo muktiṃ veda tattvataḥ | so'hamasmi na kiñcidbhūto na mṛtyurna śoko na tathā ||
verses.translation: There is one God, no second — he who knows liberation in truth. I am He, not any being, no death, no sorrow, and so on.
verses.hindi: एक ही देव है, दूसरा कोई नहीं — जो मुक्ति को तत्व से जानता है। मैं वही हूँ, कोई प्राणी नहीं, मृत्यु नहीं, शोक नहीं, वगैरह।
verses.commentary: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.
verses.wordMeaning: The affirmation of non-duality: one reality, no second. The knower recognizes "I am He" and transcends death, sorrow, and all suffering.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वत्र समदर्शित्वं सर्वभूतहिते रतिः | समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च एवं मुक्तः स उच्यते ||
verses.transliteration: sarvatra samadarśitvaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratiḥ | samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca evaṃ muktaḥ sa ucyate ||
verses.translation: One who sees equally everywhere; who is devoted to the welfare of all beings; who is the same toward enemy and friend — such a one is called liberated.
verses.hindi: जो सर्वत्र समान दृष्टि रखता है; जो सभी प्राणियों के हित में प्रीति रखता है; जो शत्रु और मित्र में समान है — ऐसे को मुक्त कहते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Muktika's portrait of the jivanmukta — and it is entirely ethical and relational. Liberation is not described in terms of meditative states, supernatural powers, or philosophical knowledge. It is described in terms of how one relates to others: samadarshitva (equal vision everywhere), sarvabhuta-hite rati (love for the welfare of all beings), sama toward enemy and friend. The liberated person is recognised not by their inner experience but by the quality of their presence in the world. This is the Muktika's most practical teaching.

verses.sanskrit: न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति | हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ||
verses.transliteration: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati | haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate ||
verses.translation: Desire is never quenched by the enjoyment of desired objects — just as fire grows ever larger when fed with oblations.
verses.hindi: कामनाएँ कामना-वस्तुओं के उपभोग से कभी शान्त नहीं होतीं — जैसे अग्नि आहुति डालने से और भी बढ़ती है।
verses.commentary: Quoted by Rama from the Manusmriti (2.94) and the Mahabharata, this verse is the Muktika's explanation of why ordinary desire-satisfaction cannot produce liberation. The fire analogy is precise: oblations (havis) are the fuel offered into the sacrificial fire, which they feed rather than extinguish. Every satisfied desire creates the template for a stronger desire. This is not an argument against enjoyment but an argument against the strategy of seeking liberation through satisfaction. The jivanmukta does not suppress desire — they no longer require its satisfaction for peace.
